Author: N.Tukaramji
Bench: N.Tukaramji
 The Honourable Sri Justice N.Tukaramji
 Criminal Petition No. 8546 Of 2025
Order

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'the BNSS') by the petitioner/de facto complainant seeking quashment of the proceedings against respondent Nos.2 and 3/accused Nos.1 and 2 in Crime No. 690 of 2023 of Panjagutta Police Station, Hyderabad District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465,
468, 471, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. I have heard Mr. P.Prabhakar Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner/de facto complainant and Mr.Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, representing respondent No.1- State.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner, who is the de facto complainant, is the father and father-in-law of respondent Nos. 2 and 3 (accused Nos. 1 and 2 respectively), both of whom currently reside in Canada.

On 7th January 2024, a Memorandum of Compromise was executed between the parties, whereby the disputed matters, including the settlement of an outstanding loan amount, were amicably resolved by respondent Nos. 2 and 3.
2 NTR,J 4.
As part of the compromise, the petitioner explicitly agreed to withdraw the pending First Information Report (FIR) upon receipt of a "No Due Certificate" from the concerned financier.
Subsequently, such a certificate was duly issued, evidencing full satisfaction of the financial obligations.
In light of this development, the petitioner no longer wishes to pursue the criminal complaint and seeks appropriate orders for closure of the matter.

5. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor, while noting that the investigation remains ongoing,
submits that in view of the settlement between the parties, suitable orders may be passed.
6. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel and perused the materials on record.

7. Having regard to the fact that the de facto complainant himself has filed the present petition stating that the disputes with respondent Nos. 2 and 3 have been amicably resolved, and that he no Shanthamaraju Mohan Rao vs State Of Telangana on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167678053/
1 longer wishes to pursue the complaint, this Court is of the considered view that continuation of the criminal proceedings would serve no useful purpose.

sentences.text: Particularly, where the complainant has voluntarily retracted his earlier allegations and the parties have reached a mutually acceptable settlement, further prosecution would be futile.

Moreover, in light of the well-settled legal principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab & Another, Anil Mishra v. State of U.P., and State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan & Others, it is well within the jurisdiction of this Court, under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, or under analogous provision Section 528 of the BNSS, to quash criminal proceedings arising out of private disputes that have been amicably settled, especially when no overriding public interest is involved.
